correctness.rationale: For an outside vertex in part i, its distance multiset is {|W|-a_i copies of 1, a_i copies of 2}; two outside vertices in distinct parts are adjacent and collide exactly when their active occupancies are equal. Fixing k active parts, k distinct nonnegative occupancies have sum at least 0+...+(k-1), with equality feasible for sorted active sizes m_j exactly when m_j>=j. For fixed k, replacing any active part by a larger one preserves feasibility and weakly decreases |W|, so the optimum uses the k largest parts, giving precisely the set K and displayed minimum. This establishes the universal formula; the verifier exhausts all multipartite isomorphism types through order eleven as a stress test. One nonessential post-proof explanatory sentence in RESULT.md says the r=2 value one comes from 'one active part with occupancy 0'; that wording is imprecise for general K_{a,b}, but the preceding criterion/formula and the conclusion lodim=1 are correct (for K_{1,1}, k=1 gives one; otherwise the feasible k=2 profile 0,1 gives one). It is not used in the proof.
residual_risks: A single nonessential explanatory sentence describing the r=2 construction is imprecisely worded; it does not affect the theorem, formula, proof, or verifier.

value.rationale: Complete multipartite graphs are a standard dense diameter-two/join family, and the local-outer parameter was introduced specifically to make such multiset identification finite. The theorem gives a complete arbitrary-part-size optimization law and cleanly separates it from the much stronger global outer invariant. This is a natural exact family result.
residual_risks: An equivalent theorem could appear under a different notation for the local outer multiset parameter in non-indexed graph-resolvability literature.

final_claim: For G=K_{n_1,...,n_r}, W is local outer multiset resolving iff the selected occupancies are pairwise distinct among active parts; sorting n_1<=...<=n_r and defining K={k: n_{r-k+j}>=j for j=1,...,k}, the exact dimension is min_{k in K}(N-sum_{i=r-k+1}^r n_i+binomial(k,2)).
scientific_limitations: An equivalent theorem could appear under a different notation for the local outer multiset parameter in non-indexed graph-resolvability literature.
The theorem is specific to complete multipartite graphs and does not classify arbitrary graph joins.
